clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 10827 (Dwight D. Eisenhower, June 25, 1959), held APP transcription, ends with the sentence "Section 1 of Executive Order No. 10685 of October 27, 1956, is hereby revoked." It states no later effective date, so the signing date June 25, 1959 is the end date.

later_events.mechanism: strike_and_insert_amendment: EO 10827 (June 25, 1959), held APP transcription, amends sections 4 and 5 of EO 10560 to read as it prints them; its section 5 reads, in the part that matters, "There are hereby reserved to the President the functions conferred upon him by section 108 of the Act, with respect to making reports to Congress." The section 5 that EO 10685 section 2 had printed also reserved the designation of the agency to receive ocean-freight funds (section 203 of the Act); the replacement text omits that reservation. It does not touch the section 6 definition and does not revoke EO 10685 section 2 as such, so it is a later event, not an end.

strike_and_insert_amendment: EO 10884 (August 17, 1960), held APP transcription, amends EO 10560 by deleting sections 1 and 5 and inserting new sections 1 and 5; the new section 5 reads "There are hereby reserved to the President the functions conferred upon him by section 108 of the Act (including that section as affected by section 406 of the Act), with respect to making reports to the Congress." It again replaces the section 5 text and leaves the section 6 definition untouched, so it is a later event, not an end.

clauses.reason: Terminated by supersession. EO 10900 (Dwight D. Eisenhower, signed January 5, 1961), held Federal Register text, section 7(a) supersedes, to the extent not already superseded, the orders in a numbered list, and item (2) of that list is EO 10685 of October 27, 1956 (the held text breaks the number and date across lines with hyphenation). EO 10900 states no later effective date, so the signing date January 5, 1961 is the end date. Section 1 of EO 10685 had already been revoked in 1959; this row is section 2.

research_rationale:
EO 10685 (October 27, 1956, Dwight D. Eisenhower), read in full in the held Federal Register text, has two sections. Section 1 designates the International Cooperation Administration as the Federal agency to which the Commodity Credit Corporation may transfer funds for ocean freight costs under Title II of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954. Section 2 rewrites sections 5 and 6 of EO 10560: section 5 reserves to the President the report-to-Congress function under section 108 and the designation function in the last sentence of section 203 of the Act, and section 6 defines the term Act. EO 10827 (June 25, 1959), held APP transcription, revokes section 1 by number; that is the first end of section 1. EO 10900 (January 5, 1961; filed January 6, 1961), held Federal Register text, section 7(a)(2), supersedes EO 10685 as a whole to the extent not already superseded; that is the first end of section 2, which EO 10827 and EO 10884 changed only by replacing the section 5 text it had printed.

savings.reason: EO 10900 section 7(b) keeps in effect actions made or taken with respect to any function it affects and not revoked, superseded or made inapplicable, except as inconsistent with it; that saving is for actions, not for the commands of this order. EO 12220 (June 27, 1980) revokes EO 10685 again among orders already superseded; it adds no end. No held source shows the ocean-freight designation or the section 6 definition operating under this order after January 5, 1961.
